title: U.S. Senate · Kansas

context.text: Incumbent Roger Marshall (R) defeated Pond Naramore in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary, 79.8% to 20.2%. Adam Hamilton won the Democratic primary in an 11-candidate field with 34.9% of the vote. David Graham advanced as the Libertarian Party's candidate.

summary.text: Roger Marshall is the Republican incumbent U.S. Senator from Kansas, first elected in 2020 after serving one term in the U.S. House representing Kansas's 1st District. He is a physician by training and serves on the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

background.text: Born in El Dorado, Kansas, in 1960.
Earned an A.S. from Butler Community College (1980), a B.S. in biochemistry from Kansas State University, and an M.D. from the University of Kansas School of Medicine (1987).
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1984 to 1991.
Worked as a physician (obstetrician) and business owner before entering politics.
Represented Kansas's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2017 to 2021 before being elected to the Senate in 2020.

positions.summary: In a February 2025 statement, Marshall backed President Trump's imposition of reciprocal tariffs.
positions.quote: Reciprocal tariffs are strong, strategic negotiating tools that ultimately strike better trade deals, ensure long-term economic growth and strengthen our national security.

positions.summary: Marshall joined Senate Republicans in introducing a resolution calling on the NCAA to revoke its transgender student-athlete eligibility policy and to protect women's sports for biological women and girls.
In a June 2026 interview, Marshall said the Senate needs to pass the SAVE America Act, discussing its voter ID and proof-of-citizenship provisions.
positions.quote: if we want to save this republic, then we need to pass the SAVE America Act.

record.text: Serves on the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

candidates.name: Adam Hamilton
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 Democratic primary in an 11-candidate field

summary.text: Adam Hamilton is a pastor from the Kansas City area running as the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. He describes himself as a fifth-generation Kansan and founder of a large United Methodist church, and campaigns on affordability, health care, and reducing corruption in Washington.

background.text: Describes himself as a fifth-generation Kansan whose family settled in Dickinson County in the 1870s.
Says he and his wife LaVon started a church with four people 36 years ago that has become the largest United Methodist church in the country.
Says the church has become the largest source of donated food in Kansas City after the regional food bank, and runs a mobile dental clinic and school-support programs.

priorities.text: Affordability: wants to end tariffs, crack down on price-gouging, expand housing construction, and pursue trade and tax policy he says would help Kansas families, farmers and small businesses.
Health care: wants to reverse Medicaid cuts he says threaten rural hospitals, restore expired ACA premium tax credits, and let Medicare negotiate more drug prices.

Government reform: supports term limits and age limits for federal officeholders, a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks, halting congressional pay during shutdowns, and says his campaign takes no corporate PAC money.

positions.summary: Hamilton's issues page calls for reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring the ACA subsidies, and expanding Medicare drug price negotiation.
positions.quote: Reverse the cuts to Medicaid and restore the ACA subsidies that hold premiums down.

positions.summary: Hamilton's issues page calls for ending tariffs and requiring congressional approval for new tariffs.
positions.quote: End self-destructive tariffs and unnecessary wars

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website was fetched directly; positions and background are drawn from Hamilton's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses. Endorsements listed on that survey: Tim Kaine, Kathleen Sebelius.

candidates.name: David Graham
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Libertarian Party of Kansas nominee
candidates.currentRole: Libertarian Party of Kansas Vice Chair

summary.text: David Graham is the Libertarian Party of Kansas Vice Chair and the party's 2026 U.S. Senate nominee. He previously ran for the same seat in 2022, receiving about 3.0% of the general-election vote.

background.text: Serves as Libertarian Party of Kansas Vice Chair.
Was the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in Kansas in 2022, receiving 29,766 votes (about 3.0% of the total) in a race won by Jerry Moran.

candidates.researchNotes: Graham has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey for 2026 or 2022, and no campaign website was found. Public record is limited to Ballotpedia election data.
